plain_language: A short description telling the captioner which subject you mean, such as “the person on the left”.
good_stuff: A short description that identifies the intended subject, such as ‘the person on the left’. It tells the caption model which subject a trigger refers to; it does not replace your concept boundary.

plain_language: The instructions for how captions should be written for the model you will train.
good_stuff: The profile of instructions that shapes caption text for the diffusion model you will train. For example, FLUX uses prose while H3 uses three named fields. Choosing a format does not make an incompatible clip or base model compatible.

plain_language: The service that runs your captioning model and manages your account access and usage.
good_stuff: The service that runs your captioning or review model. Its account grants access and determines billing. OpenAI API credits and an authorized ChatGPT plan are separate choices in this app.

plain_language: A private credential that lets ConceptStudio use your account at a service.
good_stuff: A credential that lets the app send requests under a provider account through its API (application programming interface). Usage is charged or limited by that provider. Enter the key in Settings; it is not a caption or a project instruction.

plain_language: The Mac’s protected storage for account keys and sign-in credentials.
good_stuff: macOS's protected credential storage. ConceptStudio stores provider keys and sign-in tokens there, separately from the project job, captions and exported training files.

plain_language: One service through which you can use models from several providers.
good_stuff: A service that provides one connection to models run by several providers. Select a model through the gateway and use its credential; its available models, prices and limits belong to that account.

plain_language: An optional second model that checks a proposed caption before it is saved.
good_stuff: An optional second model that checks a proposed caption against the job instructions and supplied media. It can approve or reject the caption with notes. It makes additional model requests and does not replace your review of the saved text.

plain_language: A setting controlling how much reasoning a supported model uses before answering.
good_stuff: A model's reasoning setting, when its provider supports one. More reasoning can take longer and consume more allowance. A model may keep that reasoning private; the saved result is the caption.

plain_language: A model reply organized into named fields that the app can read reliably.
good_stuff: A request for the model to return fields in a defined schema, such as usable, caption and note. The app decodes those fields before saving a caption. This controls the reply's structure, not whether its observations are correct.

plain_language: A saved version of your dataset, used to identify exactly which data a training run learned from.
good_stuff: The specific saved version of a dataset on Hugging Face, identified by a commit. A recorded revision lets a run reuse that version instead of later remote edits. Direct uploads use a digest of the local inputs instead; Resume requires those original inputs.

plain_language: The processor that does the training. In ConceptStudio it is always a cloud GPU, never the one in your Mac.
good_stuff: A graphics processing unit: the processor that runs the large caption and training models. ConceptStudio rents one or more as a cloud GPU. With one GPU, captioning and training take turns on it; with several, GPU 0 can caption while the others train.

plain_language: A graphics processor in a data centre that you rent by the hour to train your model. ConceptStudio rents it from RunPod, starts it for you, and stops it when it sits idle or reaches your spending limit. RunPod calls it a pod.
good_stuff: A RunPod pod running ConceptStudio's container image on one or more GPUs. RunPod bills it to your RunPod account while it runs. Its graphics memory, separate from your Mac's RAM, decides which models it can train. Stopping keeps its disk and any saved storage; removing it deletes its own disk. Saved storage stays, and is billed, until you delete it in RunPod.

plain_language: Storage on RunPod that you can reuse with any cloud GPU in the same data centre.
good_stuff: A RunPod network volume, billed separately to your RunPod account. It keeps datasets, checkpoints and results across stops and replacement cloud GPUs, and only cloud GPUs in its data centre can use it. Without it, ConceptStudio uses the cloud GPU's own disk, which survives stopping but is deleted when that cloud GPU is removed.

plain_language: The package of software used to start the cloud GPU, including its trainer.
good_stuff: The packaged software environment used to start the cloud GPU. It includes the control agent, trainer and required libraries. The chosen training model must have a compatible image; it is separate from your dataset and LoRA weights.

plain_language: The spending limit you set for a cloud GPU or an individual training run.
good_stuff: A GPU spending cap. The cloud GPU's limit covers the whole rental; a training run's limit covers preparation, transfer and that run's continuations. Reaching either stops the cloud GPU. Estimates exclude separately billed storage, and checks require this Mac awake with the app open.

plain_language: Start a new training run using the weights learned by an earlier LoRA.
good_stuff: Start a new training run using existing LoRA weights rather than the base model alone. The new run starts its step count at zero and uses the selected dataset. Import the matching H3 recipe and weights; this does not restore the old run's optimizer or progress.

plain_language: The model components and training settings used for a run.
good_stuff: The trainer settings used for a run, including model components, precision, optimizer and LoRA layers. Importing a supported H3 recipe preserves those choices while this project's dataset and the new run's length are selected separately.

plain_language: An optional training objective that uses an extra prediction without the caption to adjust what the model learns. It adds GPU work; the target controls the strength of that training adjustment.
good_stuff: AI Toolkit’s do_guidance_loss computes an unconditional prediction u without gradients and replaces training target t with u + g × (t − u), where g is guidance_loss_target. A two-value target samples g uniformly per example. This is a training objective; the generation guidance_scale setting is independent. The Circlestone H3 training adapter must not be combined with this objective; the Ostris adapter may be.

plain_language: Teaches the model one person’s face. Captions describe everything that can change, such as clothing, hair, expression, pose, setting and light, so you can still choose those in your prompts.
good_stuff: Target concept facial_identity with the class word “person”; the learning target is distinctive facial identity. Captions pair the trigger with the class word and describe clothing and removable accessories, hair presentation, expression and gaze, pose, setting, lighting, framing and image treatment, so those attributes stay promptable instead of being absorbed into the trigger. Images can be assigned to the person on this Mac by comparing faces with a reference photo; the captioning model can do it instead.

plain_language: Teaches the model a person’s face and build together. Their hairstyle is treated as part of who they are; clothing, expression, pose, setting and light stay changeable.
good_stuff: Target concept full_identity with the class word “person”; the learning target is the person’s enduring face and physique. Captions describe expression and gaze, pose and action, permitted clothing changes, setting, lighting and framing. Unlike Person they do not describe hair presentation, so a consistent hairstyle tends to be learned with the identity. Mapping works as for Person, including face comparison on this Mac. The concept editor offers this category when a project already uses it.

plain_language: Teaches the model a character’s whole look, such as an illustrated, animated or invented figure, including its costume and signature details. Captions describe what changes from picture to picture: pose, expression, setting and light.
good_stuff: Target concept character_design with the class word “character”; the learning target is the character’s distinctive appearance and design, costume included. Captions describe expression and gaze, pose and action, permitted clothing changes, setting, lighting and framing, so design features the captions leave out (a costume, hair, markings) are learned as part of the trigger. Choose Person instead when the subject is a real person whose outfits should stay promptable. Face comparison is not used: the captioning model or a typed location assigns the character in each image.

plain_language: Teaches the model one particular thing, such as a mug, a car or a piece of jewellery, so it can draw that exact design in new scenes.
good_stuff: Target concept object with the class word “object” (an advanced user can name a more specific noun, such as “mug”). The learning target is the object’s distinctive design. Captions describe its placement, orientation, use, surroundings, lighting and occlusion, which the model should learn as variable. Each image needs a location for the object, from the captioning model or typed by you.

plain_language: Teaches the model a way of looking, such as a painter’s brushwork, a film stock or an illustration style, which you can then apply to any subject.
good_stuff: Target concept style with the class word “style”. The trigger stands for the rendering, texture and palette shared by the images, so captions describe only the content (subject matter, objects, actions, spatial arrangement and visible scene content) and leave out the stylistic qualities to be learned. The style applies to the whole image or clip, so no per-image location is needed.

plain_language: Teaches a video model a movement, such as a dance, a gesture or a camera move. It needs video clips, because a still picture cannot show how a movement unfolds.
good_stuff: Target concept motion with the class word “motion”; the learning target is the defining movement pattern. Captions describe the performer, clothing, scene, framing, lighting and the start and end states, so the movement can transfer to other performers and settings. The motion applies to the whole clip, so no per-clip location is needed.

plain_language: Anything that doesn’t fit the other categories. You describe the concept yourself, and captions describe the visible details outside it.
good_stuff: Target concept custom with the class word “concept”. The learning target is the concept as you state it, and captions describe observable details outside that boundary. Each image needs a location for the concept. The concept editor offers this category when a project already uses it.

plain_language: The workspace where you arrange a scene, plan its movement and camera, and export a shot package.
good_stuff: Shots keeps scenes and shots in shots.json alongside the training project. Blocking, cameras, guides and prompts are prepared here for an external generation workflow.

plain_language: A shared stage containing the people, objects and movement used by one or more shots.
good_stuff: A scene owns its entities, lighting and blocking takes. Several shots can cover the same action with different cameras. Editing the shared blocking affects each shot that uses that take.

plain_language: One camera view of a scene over a chosen number of frames.
good_stuff: A shot references a blocking take and owns its camera marks, frame count, canvas, guide frames, notes and prompt. Several shots can reuse the same scene action.

plain_language: The planned positions and movement of people and objects in a scene.
good_stuff: Blocking uses timed actor marks to describe positions, holds, travel, facing and actions. A shared blocking take can be filmed by more than one shot camera.

plain_language: A timed instruction for where an actor or camera should be and what it should do.
good_stuff: An actor mark stores position, gait, facing and optional pose or boarding changes. A camera mark stores position, angles and lens settings. Easing controls the transition between marks; hold controls when it leaves.

plain_language: How long an actor or camera stays at a mark before moving on.
good_stuff: Hold is measured in seconds after reaching the mark. The evaluator shortens a hold that would overlap the next mark so the next movement still has time to happen.

plain_language: The kind of movement or pose an actor uses, such as walking, running or sitting.
good_stuff: The gait on a destination mark selects the movement used while approaching that mark. At a held mark it selects the base pose. Motion presets can add joint overrides, and uniform scale changes the stride.

plain_language: A still image from a chosen frame that helps guide the generated shot.
good_stuff: The first frame and last frame are included automatically, along with any extra interior guide frames. Frame indices start at zero and identify the exact corresponding video frame in the package.

plain_language: The files you take to a ComfyUI workflow to generate a planned shot.
good_stuff: A package carries the selected clean reference, pose and layout videos, actor mattes, matching guide stills, shot description and manifest. It also contains prompt text and structured prompt data when a prompt has been written.

plain_language: The model’s allowed spacing for the number of frames in a shot.
good_stuff: Frame counts follow 17k + 5: 5, 22, 39 and so on. Shots snaps frame-count edits to this grid. The trained range is 124–362 frames; the frame rate is 24 frames per second.

plain_language: The width and height, in pixels, of the shot’s exported images and videos.
good_stuff: The canvas fixes the image aspect ratio and export dimensions. Custom dimensions use multiples of 32 pixels. It is separate from the dimensions of the editor viewport or the physical size of the scene.

plain_language: The view through the shot’s camera, showing the framing you plan to export.
good_stuff: Look-through uses the same frame renderer, scene look and shot camera as the clean export. The image is letterboxed to the shot canvas; the free editor camera can show a different view of the scene.

plain_language: Keeps the shot camera pointed at selected subjects as they move.
good_stuff: With one subject, the camera aims at that subject. With several, it aims at their midpoint. Aim lock controls pointing; a camera mount separately makes the camera ride with an entity.
